images.caption: Aerial view of Hadleigh Castle and Country Park Hadleigh Castle is not actually in the country park (which is probably why they changed the name from 'Hadleigh Castle Country Park' to 'Hadleigh Country Park'). This view shows the remains of the castle on a mound overlooking the estuary. In its heyday, the castle would have been right next to the estuary. Today, the middle distance is occupied by Hadleigh Marsh. The area of this beyond the railway line (across the centre) is now used for growing vegetables. Beyond this, near the top centre, the triangular pool is at the western tip of Two-Tree Island. Since this photo was taken, this pool has been colonised by Avocets, and these have recently bred successfully there.

images.caption: Hadleigh Castle (5) This castle dates from 1230 and was originally built for King John.  It is in a state of ruins because Edward VI sold off the stone so it could be used elsewhere.  English Heritage now own the site.  Extensive work has taken place on the castle over the last two years to stop it crumbling away.  This is the first visit I have made where the scaffolding has been removed.  Please see my other photos of the castle.

images.caption: Acorn Street is a historic and picturesque cobblestone street located in the renowned Beacon Hill neighborhood of Boston, Massachusetts, USA. This charming street has become a beloved attraction, drawing visitors from near and far. Acorn Street is characterized by its well-preserved row houses, constructed in brick and stone, which exude a timeless elegance. The street's gas lamps, quaint flower boxes, and narrow layout create a nostalgic ambiance, evoking the charm of the 19th century. Particularly during the autumn season, Acorn Street's beauty reaches new heights, as the vibrant foliage of the trees that line the street transforms into a stunning tapestry of red and orange hues. Although Acorn Street is a popular destination for tourists, its appeal extends beyond its visual splendor. The street provides a glimpse into Boston's rich history and serves as a living testament to the city's architectural heritage. Whether strolling along the cobblestones or admiring the captivating facades, a visit to Acorn Street offers a truly immersive experience in the heart of Boston's cultural tapestry.
